seoTitle: How to Add Multiple Quantity to an eBay Listing
metaDescription: Learn how to add bulk quantity to a single eBay listing in 2026 so buyers can purchase multiple units without creating separate listings.
intro: If you're selling identical items in bulk, adding multiple quantity to one listing saves you from creating duplicate posts and keeps your inventory organized. This guide covers how to set this up for a fixed-price eBay listing.

steps.heading: Start a fixed-price listing
steps.body: Multiple quantity options are available for fixed-price listings rather than auction-style ones, so choose that format when creating or editing your listing.

steps.heading: Set the quantity field
steps.body: Enter the total number of identical units you have available for sale under the quantity field during listing creation.

steps.heading: Let buyers select how many they want
steps.body: Once live, buyers can choose the quantity they'd like to purchase directly from your single listing page.

steps.heading: Track inventory automatically
steps.body: eBay reduces your available quantity automatically as units sell, helping you avoid manually updating stock after each sale.

steps.heading: Avoid overselling with correct limits
steps.body: Keep your quantity number accurate and update it promptly if your actual stock changes outside of eBay sales, to avoid selling more than you have.

faq.question: Can I add multiple quantity to an auction-style eBay listing?
faq.answer: No, multiple quantity is only available for fixed-price 'Buy It Now' listings, not traditional auction-style listings.

faq.question: Does eBay automatically update my stock count as items sell?
faq.answer: Yes, the listed quantity decreases automatically with each sale, helping prevent you from accidentally overselling.

faq.question: Can I use multiple quantity with Good 'Til Cancelled listings?
faq.answer: Yes, this feature works with Good 'Til Cancelled listings, which is helpful for ongoing bulk inventory.

faq.question: Is adding bulk quantity better than creating separate listings?
faq.answer: Yes, it keeps your store cleaner, consolidates buyer interest into one listing, and simplifies inventory tracking compared to multiple duplicate listings.
